problem: Existing compositional zero-shot learning methods use simple composition-prototype mapping that doesn't account for diverse semantic subsets, and ignore compositional divergence within identical states or objects.
approach: EVA introduces a mixture-of-experts framework with domain-expert adaptation for token-aware learning and semantic variant alignment to select semantically relevant representations for image-primitives matching.
contribution: EVA significantly outperforms state-of-the-art CZSL methods on three benchmarks in both closed- and open-world settings.

problem: Universal image restoration requires removing various degradations while preserving high-quality image detail and adjusting outputs based on degradation type and level.
approach: BDG proposes a multi-stage diffusion approach combining a novel Multi-Angle and multi-Scale Gray Level Co-occurrence Matrix (MAS-GLCM) for fine-grained degradation discrimination, then integrating this information into a three-stage diffusion pipeline (generation, bridging, restoration).
contribution: BDG achieves significant performance gains in all-in-one restoration and real-world super-resolution without architecture changes, improving fidelity while preserving perceptual quality.

problem: Diffusion large language models offer parallel token prediction but still require nearly token-length decoding steps for performance, limiting their inference speed advantage.
approach: dParallel introduces certainty-forcing distillation, a training strategy that distills models to follow original sampling trajectories while enforcing rapid parallel convergence to high certainty on masked tokens.
contribution: dParallel reduces decoding steps from 256 to 30 on GSM8K (8.5x speedup) and from 256 to 24 on MBPP (10.5x speedup) without performance degradation.

problem: Multiple reasoning LLMs should collaborate on shared reasoning trajectories for better efficiency, but standard solo-reasoning training doesn't yield off-trajectory behaviors where models can assess and build on others' partial thinking.
approach: The paper proposes twin tests (Recoverability and Guidability) to evaluate whether LLMs can backtrack from misleading reasoning and leverage guiding steps from collaborators, testing 15 open-weight models (1.5B-32B).
contribution: Stronger LLMs are often more fragile under distraction, and all tested models fail to leverage guiding steps beyond their inherent capabilities (solve rates under 9.2%), with insights on distillation teacher choice, RL, and data selection affecting these behaviors.

problem: Continual learning requires balancing knowledge preservation and transfer to future tasks while minimizing forgetting, but general-purpose upper bounds on learning plasticity are lacking.
approach: The paper extends PAC-Bayes bounds from online learning to continual learning, deriving general upper bounds on cumulative generalization loss applicable to any task distribution and learning algorithm, with oracle bounds for Gibbs posteriors.
contribution: Non-vacuous PAC-Bayes bounds achieved on several continual learning vision problems and tight oracle bounds on linear regression, with this being the first general upper bound on learning plasticity for continual learning.

problem: Personalizing LLMs for individual user preferences faces challenges in obtaining accurate user-specific reward signals in open-ended scenarios, as existing models oversimplify preferences and struggle generalizing to new users with limited feedback.
approach: P-GenRM transforms preference signals into structured evaluation chains, derives adaptive personas and scoring rubrics, clusters users into prototypes, and employs dual-granularity scaling (individual-level and prototype-level) to enhance generalization.
contribution: P-GenRM achieves state-of-the-art results with ~2.31% average improvement on personalized reward benchmarks and demonstrates strong generalization on out-of-distribution data, with test-time user-based scaling providing an additional ~3% boost.

problem: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) applies uniform optimization across all image tokens in autoregressive generation, but different tokens contribute differently to training and remain unexplored.
approach: GCPO identifies critical tokens from three perspectives: causal dependency of early tokens, entropy-induced spatial structure, and RLVR-focused token diversity, then applies dynamic token-wise advantage weighting based on confidence divergence.
contribution: By leveraging only 30% of image tokens, GCPO achieves better performance than GRPO with full tokens on multiple benchmarks.

problem: Density estimation from pairwise comparisons requires relating unobserved target densities to observable winner distributions (marginal of preferred choices) for applications like expert knowledge elicitation and learning from human feedback.
approach: The method learns the winner density via score-matching and de-tempers to estimate the target; derives collinearity between belief and winner density score vectors linked by position-dependent tempering field, with analytical formulas under Bradley-Terry model.
contribution: The approach enables learning complex multivariate belief densities from hundreds to thousands of pairwise comparisons using diffusion models trained on tempered samples.

problem: Real-world degradations make correspondences between low-quality and reference images unreliable, leading to reference-based super-resolution methods over-relying on misleading references or under-utilizing valuable cues.
approach: Ada-RefSR proposes Adaptive Implicit Correlation Gating (AICG) that employs learnable summary tokens to distill dominant reference patterns and capture implicit correlations with low-quality features, providing adaptive regulation of reference guidance.
contribution: Ada-RefSR achieves strong balance of fidelity, naturalness, and efficiency while remaining robust under varying reference alignment across multiple datasets.

problem: Parallel token generation in arbitrary-order models violates conditional independence assumptions needed for accurate distribution matching, while discrete diffusion models struggle with parallel generation accuracy.
approach: Any-Subset Autoregressive Models (AS-ARMs) can generate tokens in any order and parallel, supporting parallelized joint probability density estimation; Any-Subset Speculative Decoding (ASSD) corrects parallel-generated distributions via the model's own joint probability estimation.
contribution: ASSD provably enables correct joint distribution generation with neural network calls upper bounded by predicted token count, achieves state-of-the-art on sub-200M models for infilling, and nearly matches 50X larger models on code generation.

problem: Long-form music generation, particularly lyrics-to-song, requires maintaining lyrical alignment, coherent musical structure, and engaging melodies over extended sequences.
approach: YuE introduces track-decoupled next-token prediction to overcome dense mixture signals and structural progressive conditioning for long-context lyrical alignment, redesigning in-context learning for bidirectional music generation including style cloning.
contribution: YuE scales to trillions of tokens generating up to five minutes of music, matching or exceeding proprietary systems in musicality and vocal agility as of January 2025.

problem: Modeling 3D dynamics in multi-body systems typically depends on explicitly observed structures and fails to capture unobserved interactions crucial to complex physical behaviors.
approach: PAINET proposes SE(3)-equivariant architecture comprising physics-inspired attention derived from energy function minimization and a parallel decoder preserving equivariance while enabling efficient inference.
contribution: PAINET consistently outperforms recent models on human motion capture, molecular dynamics, and protein simulations with 4.7% to 41.5% error reductions in 3D dynamics prediction at comparable computational cost.

problem: Masked diffusion LLMs face an exploration challenge in reinforcement learning: sparse reward signals and sample waste when models fail to discover correct solutions.
approach: IGPO introduces Inpainting Guided Policy Optimization, strategically inserting partial ground-truth reasoning traces during online sampling to guide exploration while preserving self-generated reasoning, combined with synthetic trace rewriting and entropy-based filtering.
contribution: IGPO achieves new state-of-the-art results on GSM8K, Math500, AMC, and Minerva benchmarks for full-attention masked dLLMs with substantial gains across mathematical reasoning tasks.

problem: LLMs have been extensively studied for memory ability, but their capacity for selective forgetting during inference without parameter updates remains largely unexplored.
approach: ICF-Bench introduces a comprehensive benchmark for In-Context Forgetting comprising 2k multi-turn dialogues, testing whether LLMs can selectively forget interference information while retaining useful knowledge.
contribution: Advanced LLMs perform well without interference but struggle significantly when interference is present, with stronger memory not translating to stronger in-context forgetting capacity and context length having differential effects across scenarios.

problem: Attention-based regression models jointly optimizing MSE and Pearson correlation show a PCC plateau phenomenon where correlation stops improving early while MSE continues decreasing, revealing fundamental optimization and capacity limitations.
approach: The paper provides theoretical analysis of the PCC plateau, revealing conflict between magnitude-matching (MSE) and shape-matching (PCC) objectives exacerbated by softmax attention; proposes Extrapolative Correlation Attention (ECA) with mechanisms to improve optimization and extrapolate beyond convex hull.
contribution: ECA breaks the PCC plateau across diverse benchmarks including homogeneous data, achieving significant correlation improvements without compromising MSE performance.

problem: Evaluating AI model capabilities on real-world economically valuable knowledge-work tasks requires comprehensive benchmarks covering diverse occupations and work activities aligned with industry standards.
approach: GDPval constructs tasks from representative work of 14-year-average-experience professionals across 44 occupations in top 9 GDP-contributing sectors, with frontier model evaluation and automated grading service.
contribution: Frontier model performance improves linearly over time and approaches industry experts in deliverable quality; increased reasoning, task context, and scaffolding improve performance, with gold subset of 220 tasks open-sourced.

problem: While reinforcement learning shows superior performance for improving complex reasoning in LLMs, its impact on cross-lingual generalization compared to supervised fine-tuning remains unexplored.
approach: Systematic investigation using Qwen2.5-3B-Base on diverse multilingual reasoning benchmarks (math, commonsense, scientific) with mechanistic analysis of RL's superiority.
contribution: RL achieves higher accuracy and substantially stronger cross-lingual generalization than SFT; training on non-English data with RL yields better overall performance and generalization than English training, not observed with SFT.

problem: Bimanual manipulation requires learning efficiently from minimal demonstrations while adapting to real-world uncertainties, balancing extensive demonstration needs against modular methods' lack of dynamic adaptability.
approach: VLBiMan derives reusable skills from single human examples via task-aware decomposition preserving invariant primitives as anchors while dynamically adapting components through vision-language grounding with semantic parsing and geometric feasibility constraints.
contribution: VLBiMan drastically reduces demonstration requirements, demonstrates compositional generalization through skill splicing, shows robustness to novel objects and disturbances, and enables strong cross-embodiment transfer without retraining.

problem: MLLMs face computational overhead processing long videos due to massive visual tokens; existing token reduction methods focus on redundancy but neglect content changes and turning points critical for understanding video dynamics.
approach: ST-SimDiff constructs spatio-temporal graphs from visual tokens and employs dual-selection: similarity-based selection uses community detection for redundancy compression, temporal difference-based selection identifies content-changing points via graph analysis.
contribution: ST-SimDiff significantly outperforms state-of-the-art video understanding approaches while substantially reducing computational costs with minimal token count.

problem: MLLMs struggle with hour-long video understanding due to input token capacity constraints, while existing approaches require costly training procedures hindering adaptability to rapidly evolving MLLM architectures.
approach: Proposes training-free framework combining Adaptive Frame Sampling (increasing density in relevant segments), Dynamic Resolution Allocation (reducing resolution in less relevant segments), and Video-Query-Options Similarity (generating candidate answers to refine relevance).
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on 5 mainstream benchmarks through training-free approach on LLaVA-Video and Qwen2.5-VL with significant computational efficiency improvements.

problem: Online RL algorithms like GRPO cannot learn from problems too difficult for models to solve, as no reward signals arise when exploration never produces correct solutions, preventing improvement on hard samples.
approach: NuRL proposes nudging method using self-generated hints (abstract cues reducing problem difficulty) during online RL training; hints are injected for hard samples with 0% pass rate to enable learning from previously unsolvable problems.
contribution: NuRL unlocks learning from hard samples and pushes the upper bound of LLM reasoning by enabling meaningful gradients and improved sample efficiency for previously unsolvable problems.

problem: RAG systems suffer from faithfulness failures where generations contradict or extend beyond provided sources; existing hallucination detection methods rely on large-scale training or expensive external LLM judges with limited accuracy.
approach: RAGLens leverages sparse autoencoders to disentangle internal LLM activations identifying hallucination-specific features; employs systematic pipeline of information-based feature selection and additive feature modeling for lightweight detection.
contribution: RAGLens achieves superior hallucination detection compared to existing methods while providing interpretable rationales for its decisions through mechanistic interpretability, enabling effective post-hoc mitigation.

problem: Multi-view 3D reconstruction suffers from photometric inconsistencies across views due to on-device camera processing (exposure, white balance, color correction), violating consistency constraints.
approach: CHROMA proposes generalizable feed-forward approach predicting spatially adaptive bilateral grids to correct photometric variations; uses hybrid self-supervised rendering loss leveraging 3D foundation models for generalization.
contribution: CHROMA outperforms or matches scene-specific optimization methods with appearance modeling while processing hundreds of frames in single step and enabling cross-scene generalization without scene-specific retraining.

problem: Existing exploratory bonus methods in RLHF unintentionally bias exploration toward high-probability regions of reference models under KL or alpha-divergence regularization, reinforcing conservative behavior.
approach: GEB proposes General Exploratory Bonus framework provably satisfying optimism principle via reference-dependent reward regulation, unifying prior bonuses as special cases while extending across full alpha-divergence family.
contribution: GEB consistently outperforms baselines on alignment tasks across multiple divergence settings and LLM backbones, offering principled solution for optimistic exploration in RLHF.

problem: Virtual cell models function as black boxes offering predictions without interpretability or consistency with biological principles, limiting their credibility; generalization remains constrained by data quality and batch effects.
approach: VCWorld integrates structured biological knowledge with LLM iterative reasoning to instantiate a white-box simulator operating in data-efficient manner reproducing perturbation-induced signaling cascades.
contribution: VCWorld achieves state-of-the-art drug perturbation prediction performance with interpretable stepwise predictions and mechanistic hypotheses consistent with publicly available biological evidence.

problem: Evaluating robot control policies is difficult: real-world testing is costly and handcrafted simulators require manual effort to improve realism and generality.
approach: WorldGym proposes autoregressive action-conditioned video generation model as proxy environment; policies evaluated via Monte Carlo rollouts with vision-language model providing rewards.
contribution: Policy success rates in world model highly correlate with real-world success rates and preserve relative policy rankings; enables efficient evaluation of generalization on novel tasks with only single start frame as input.

problem: Dynamically configuring algorithm hyperparameters is fundamental but learning-based methods suffer from prohibitive sample complexity and poor generalization, while existing approaches require training.
approach: AutoEP leverages LLMs as zero-shot reasoning engines combining online Exploratory Landscape Analysis providing real-time feedback with multi-LLM reasoning chain generating adaptive hyperparameter strategies.
contribution: AutoEP consistently outperforms state-of-the-art tuners including neural evolution and other LLM-based methods on three metaheuristics; open-source models like Qwen3-30B match GPT-4 performance.

problem: Large Reasoning Models generate extended reasoning traces often exhibiting substantial redundancy, limiting inference efficiency; promoting reasoning efficiency via RL remains underexplored.
approach: LASER proposes Length-based Adaptive Step-wise Reward shaping using step function based on target length, further extended as LASER-D to dynamically adapt rewards and apply difficulty-aware penalization of lengthy CoTs.
contribution: LASER-D significantly enhances reasoning performance and response length efficiency on five open-weight models (1.5B-32B) by combining fast and slow thinking for better overall trade-off.

problem: Machine-learned operators claiming zero-shot super-resolution fail to generalize across resolutions due to inability to extrapolate to varying frequency information and interpolate across resolutions.
approach: The paper comprehensively evaluates MLO multi-resolution inference, decoupling into frequency extrapolation and resolution interpolation; proposes simple computationally-efficient multi-resolution training protocol addressing aliasing.
contribution: Proposed training protocol enables robust multi-resolution generalization, overcoming MLO brittleness and susceptibility to aliasing demonstrated through comprehensive empirical evaluation.

problem: Multi-modal large language models lag in reasoning due to outdated internal LLMs; upgrading is prohibitively expensive requiring complete vision-language alignment retraining.
approach: RAPID introduces Perception-Reasoning Decoupling modularizing MLLM's reasoning component for easy replacement; proposes Visual Perception Optimization (VPO) using external reasoner correctness as reward to align MLLM's perceptual output.
contribution: RAPID achieves significant performance gains on multi-modal reasoning benchmarks and enables novel inference-time scaling: MLLM can be paired with state-of-the-art reasoners for consistent improvement without retraining.

problem: Scarcity of high-quality training data limits information-seeking agent development; existing synthesis approaches lead to inconsistency between information and reasoning structure.
approach: WebShaper proposes formalization-driven synthesis framework using set-theoretic Knowledge Projections enabling precise reasoning structure control; agentic Expander expands formal questions through retrieval and validation.
contribution: WebShaper achieves state-of-the-art performance among open-source information-seeking agents on competitive benchmarks through systematic task formalization and multi-step expansion.

problem: Prioritized Experience Replay effectively samples experiences for efficient RL learning but lacks reliability measure for temporal difference errors, limiting optimality of selection.
approach: ReaPER extends PER with novel temporal difference error reliability measure; the resulting transition selection algorithm enables more efficient learning than PER.
contribution: ReaPER outperforms uniform experience replay and PER on diverse environments including classic control and Atari-10 benchmark, matching median Atari-57 score within one percent variance.

problem: In AI-assisted decision-making, existing confidence adjustment objectives like calibration and human-alignment are insufficient to ensure fair utility across heterogeneous decision-maker groups with varying cognitive capacities.
approach: Introduces inter-group-alignment concept to ensure fair utility; proposes multicalibration-based confidence adjustment approach addressing both human-alignment and inter-group-alignment objectives.
contribution: Establishes interpretable fairness-aware objective for AI confidence adjustment; demonstrates through theoretical and empirical analysis that utility fairness requires both human-alignment and inter-group-alignment.

problem: Self-Consistency inference for LLM reasoning is computationally expensive, fully expanding all reasoning traces despite many sharing similar early reasoning patterns.
approach: PoLR clusters short reasoning prefixes to identify dominant patterns, expands only promising paths while leveraging prefix self-consistency; theoretical analysis via mutual information explains why early steps encode strong correctness signals.
contribution: PoLR matches or exceeds Self-Consistency accuracy on GSM8K, Math500, AIME 2024/2025, and GPQA-Diamond while reducing token usage by up to 60% and latency by up to 50%.

problem: Prevailing contrastive methods for training LLMs as text encoders treat models as black-box functions, discarding generative and reasoning capabilities in favor of static embeddings.
approach: GRACE reimagines contrastive signals as rewards guiding generative policy where LLM produces explicit human-interpretable rationales explaining semantic understanding; rationales encoded into embeddings via policy gradient optimization.
contribution: GRACE yields 11.5% supervised and 6.9% unsupervised performance improvement on MTEB benchmark across backbones while preserving capabilities and providing transparent reasoning traces.

problem: Inference-time reward models can impair simple question performance, show declining discriminative ability with increased sampling, and perform poorly under high search diversity.
approach: CRISP clusters reasoning paths by final answers, aggregates reward signals at cluster level, and adaptively updates prefix prompts to guide generation.
contribution: CRISP achieves up to 5% accuracy improvement over other reward-model-based inference methods and average 10% gain over advanced reasoning models.

problem: Lower-resource languages lack fluent preference-aligned language models due to scarcity of native-speaker datasets and models incapable of generating fluent synthetic data.
approach: Proposes on-policy training method for preference alignment that preserves fluency without instruction-tuning data in target language, compared against supervised fine-tuning on machine-translated data and multilingual fine-tuning.
contribution: On-policy approach outperforms alternatives for Norwegian Bokmål as verified by native-speaker fluency assessments, demonstrating crucial importance of on-policy training for lower-resource languages.

problem: How to explicitly steer training toward exploration or exploitation in Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) for reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards remains an open problem.
approach: Introduces Token Hidden Reward (THR) metric quantifying each token's influence on correct response likelihood; tokens with positive THR strengthen confidence (exploitation) while negative THR preserve alternatives (exploration).
contribution: THR-guided reweighting algorithm enables explicit bias toward exploitation (improving greedy accuracy) or exploration (Pass@K gains) and integrates with GSPO, generalizing across architectures.

problem: Federated fine-tuning of LLMs enables privacy-preserving adaptation but resource-intensive nature severely limits deployment on edge devices.
approach: DevFT decomposes fine-tuning into developmental stages optimizing submodels with increasing capacity, using deconfliction-guided layer grouping and differential-based layer fusion for efficiency.
contribution: DevFT achieves up to 4.59x faster convergence, 10.67x communication overhead reduction, and 9.07% performance improvement while maintaining federated fine-tuning compatibility.

problem: Vision-language systems process images holistically with limited support for explicit compositional decomposition; previous decomposition methods rely on hand-crafted inductive biases rather than learning.
approach: CRD framework uses large vision-language models to propose visual concepts and values instantiating concept rule functions modeling concept changes; iteratively selects concise concepts best accounting for input.
contribution: CRD outperforms baselines on abstract reasoning benchmark and real-world image captions while improving interpretability by explicitly revealing underlying concepts and compositional rules.
